mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but SPX returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment below 3.5% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE below 3.5% but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising CPI and industrial production indicate inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as the Fed may tighten rates.
failure_condition: Both CPI and INDPRO rise but SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates lead to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS rise but SPX returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: PAYEMS increases but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 1200 indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: HOUST above 1200 but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales and low unemployment indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: RSAFS rises and UNRATE is low but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth in late expansion indicates sustained economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth is positive but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.
